unit: X1 and the measuring half of X3 of docs/plans/SELF_PROOF_EXECUTION_PLAN_2026-11-12.md
claim: measurement only. A BYTE_EQUAL row says one program printed pinned Lean's bytes through that lane. It is not a codegen license, covers no other program, and makes no item of the plan's section 2.1 hold.
how_to_read: `programs` pins what each lane does with each fixture program, and for the R4 probes what `clean check` (Clean's elaborator and kernel, no backend) does; the test fails when a live outcome differs. A lane outcome is BYTE_EQUAL, a refusal by name (REFUSED_BUILD, REFUSED_RUNTIME, EMIT_TRUSTIR_REFUSED, TRUSTCG_REFUSED, LINK_FAILED) or CRASHED (the process died on a signal after printing a prefix of Lean's bytes; a crash is not a refusal and is pinned only so its gap is listed). `gaps` is the burn-down list: one row per construct a lane refuses or crashes on, with the refusing source site. `lane_shortfalls` lists what the trust-cg lane does not give even where it prints the right bytes. `r4_items` maps the ten items of risk R4 of designs/2026-11-12-kcheck-model-first.md to their probes. `rejected_by_lean` pins `clean check` on programs pinned Lean rejects (the negative controls), and `false_acceptances` owns each of those Clean accepts. `closed_in_this_unit` records what was refused when the unit began and is not any more. A refusal that closes fails the test; retire its gap and re-pin the row in the same change.

Fresh six-control/compiled-stack captures share that exact source and binary identity. Five structural parity forms and five Lean-rejected hint controls pass; the pre-existing bare-constructor false acceptance remains owned below. The original c36 acceptance was invalid because three clauses were recovered away; current c36 has nine declarations and zero recovery. The audit owns compiler repair. No full workspace, formal proof, semantic soundness, quorum or release claim.

summary.checker: advice_replay: BYTE_EQUAL on both lanes. Its mutant advice_replay_no_compare: BYTE_EQUAL on both lanes, which is Lean's bytes for the mutant, accepting three corrupted cases.
summary.r4_items: The current primary probes include true call cycles c34/c35/c36 for (i)/(ix)/(x); pinned Lean accepts all ten and every cycle member uses every _f auxiliary with Nat.brecOn. The original capture had only eight recovery-free acceptances because c36 dropped three structural clauses. After the 2026-11-14 parser and explicit-major fixes, all ten are rechecked recovery-aware: nine accepted, vii refused for absent ByteArray. See reports/x1-recheck/README.md; the original nine-pass claim was invalid. Both backends: i, ii, iii, vi, ix byte-equal; iv and x SIGSEGV; v and viii refused at lowering; vii refused at elaboration. The old c24/c32/c33 remain acyclic controls. The fenced ReferenceKernel re-check for vi remains unmeasured.

gaps.construct: a self tail call on Nat compiled as recursive closure applications rather than a loop, overflowing the compiled program stack
gaps.needed_for: Design 3.2 and R4 (iv), (x): a self tail call must compile to a loop on both lanes for kcheck depth-counter recursion. At 8 MiB, both Clean lanes print Lean bytes at 10,000 steps and SIGSEGV at 100,000 and 1,000,000. Both lanes print the full expected 100,000-step bytes at 65,520 KiB; the million-step c27 and c36 still overflow there. Pinned Lean compiled binaries of all three exit 0 at 8 MiB, byte-equal to lean --run, with self tail calls emitted as goto _start. This identifies a compiled-program stack overflow in Clean, not an upstream Lean overflow or an exact crash threshold.
gaps.stage: clean-compiler, the lowering of `Nat.rec` (structural recursion) to a synthesized local recursive function: it returns a closure per step (`_rec_0(pred)`) that the caller applies with `clean_apply_n` and then releases its arguments, so the recursive call is neither a direct call nor in tail position
gaps.refusal: clean run: program terminated by signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
gaps.refusal_seen_with: clean run <program> --decl main (both lanes; the program prints nothing before the crash). The emitted C is `clean compile <program> --decl headLoop --emit c -o <file>`.
gaps.fix_scope: not local: structural recursion whose motive is a function type compiled as a direct self-recursive function (Lean's compiler does this from the equation compiler's output, not from the recursor), with RC that leaves the self call in tail position, and a C or trust-cg emission of that tail call as a jump. Falsifies R4 (iv) on both backends today.

lane_shortfalls.what: every body of every program is stamped `clean-compiler-unvalidated`; none carries a kernel-TV certificate. trust-cg emits them only because the invocation recognizes that authority. The plan's section 2.1 asks that every body be licensed.
lane_shortfalls.pinned_by: the trust-cg test asserts kernel_tv_certified == 0 for every built program

lane_shortfalls.what: the runtime, the prelude shims and the entry driver are C, compiled and linked by the host `cc`. Only the program's own bodies go through trust-ir and trust-cg. The plan's section 2.1 asks for no C path.
lane_shortfalls.pinned_by: the trust-cg test asserts the receipt's `runtime` is "C via cc"

lane_shortfalls.what: both lanes share Clean's elaborator and clean-compiler down to L5IR, so byte-equality between them is not an independent check of anything above the emitter, and every gap above the emitter refuses both.
lane_shortfalls.pinned_by: the `programs` rows: each gap in `gaps` is cited on both lanes
